title: Pandolfo Malatesta, archbishop of Patras (Rome), to Gianfrancesco Gonzaga, 22 Apr 1428, Archivio di Stato di Mantova (DECODE R1854 image 1)

steps.what: Fetched R1854 (5 images), the R1853 register (14 images) and DECODE metadata with the saved cookie.
Web search for Pandolfo Malatesta's ciphered letters (Treccani DBI; Falcioni 2015 prints the plaintext of his 1438 cipher letter, ASMn AG b. 1081).
Read the R1853 register keys (Malatesta keys on f. 1, 1406-1419 keys): none match the 1428-30 letters.
Opened all other Mantova records on DECODE (R7858-R7888): 16th-17th century keys.
P1 cipher runs transcribed (266 signs).
P1 anneals in Latin and Italian, with and without spaces, costed nulls, vowel constraint, reversed orders, split and merged digraphs: no reading.
Solver reads a synthetic 266-letter monoalphabetic Latin text, also with 12% token noise: P1 is not a simple substitution in Latin.
Register key 'cum Malatesta dni Pandulfi' values seeded into the P1 anneal: -4.2/char, no fit.
Subagent second pass of P1 (262 signs, 3 runs, 3 misreadings fixed) and clear-text transcription.
P1 re-solved from the second pass in Latin, Italian and modern Italian: no reading.

P1: digraphic test (sign-pair IC 0.005, no), periodicity test (column IC flat for periods 2-8, not polyalphabetic), vowel/consonant alternation 0.713 above all 200 shuffles (linear text, not transposed).
P1 annealed in Spanish, Catalan, French, German, Portuguese, and with order-3 Latin/Italian models over 150 restarts: no reading.
Opened DECODE R1855 (Modena Este keys, incl. Malatesta Novello 1441) and R1852 (Florence Dieci keys 1424-32): sign sets differ from P1, no fit.
P1 syllable-aware anneal (each sign a letter, one of 27 common Latin/Italian syllables or word signs, or null; frequency prior): no reading.
Images re-fetched from DECODE with the saved cookie (PNG, P1 1121x697 px); P1 run lines cropped at 3x, L05 matches p1v2.txt sign for sign.

P1 annealed with the separators kept as cipher signs (// : ... . | as five extra signs, p1_withsep.txt), Latin and Italian, 10 restarts each: best -2.76 (la) and -2.63 (it-cinquecento) per char, no words; separators are not hidden letters.
Split from the R1854 entry under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): the record's four letters use four ciphers; image 1 is this entry, not solved.

Outside reading received by email (Mark Vladimir Prizmic, with Claude, from Satoshi Tomokiyo's 309-sign transcription and CTTS trial): all three runs Latin, homophonic substitution with two nulls (Tomokiyo's v and g), north-Italian x for s. Run 1: de suis gentibus armigeris cassandis vel quid aliud peragendum [one sign unread] delliberet; run 2: absque discrimine et multo dispendio provincie Moree, patrie siquidem fertilis et amene, rex effici; run 3: De eo autem regno magnificum comitem Riciardum bene informatum puto, quoniam ad illud cum serenissima sorore nostra domina vaxilissa tetendit, et iterum deinde etiam sui ocaxione redivit. Five corrections to Tomokiyo's transcription, which Tomokiyo accepted. His key table and transcription (the email attachment) are not yet checked here.
Received Prizmic's key (key.json: 31 sign values, nulls v and g, sign 23 unread) and the corrected transcription (308 signs) as email attachments; saved in the target folder with their source.

Applied the key to the corrected transcription with dec.py: the three decoded runs agree letter for letter with the reading (66, 82 and 160 signs, 307 of 308 read, one unread). Control: under the Latin model 'la' the decode scores -5.25 per letter against -6.90 for the best of 300 keys with the letters shuffled among the sign classes (mean -7.88); lm.best_language names Latin (-2.18, ahead of every other language). The reading also fits the clear text round each run (run 2 follows 'me sciat quo modo valeat', run 3 leads into 'amplitudinem tantam vendicare ... sibi et natis'), and the first and last words of run 1 agree sign for sign with our own p1v2.txt. Not an independent decipherment: the key was built with the reading, and the control shuffles an already-fitted key.

Built the decoded runs and the clear Latin of the letter into one text (texts/p1_decryption.md) and an English translation (texts/p1_en.md); the sentences hold, with doubts only in the clear transcription (prepositum(?), fratrem(?), sensu(?)) and the one unread sign.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Prizmic's key (built with Claude from Tomokiyo's transcription and a Latin model, then fitted by hand) was applied to the corrected transcription here: all 307 read signs decode to the reading, which scores -5.25 per letter in Latin against -6.90 for the best of 300 shuffled keys, and fits the clear text round each run.
outcome.fraction_read_source: dec.py: 307 of 308 signs decoded; sign 23 (once) unread

gaps.detail: the sentence is complete without it, so it may be a null; one sign, no other occurrence to compare

outcome.notes: Split 14 Oct 2026 from the four-letter R1854 entry; catalogue entry 152. Not solved here: the first reading is Prizmic's (5 Nov 2026). Open outside the cipher: Count Riciardo is not identified, and the clear text round runs 1 and 2 wants a better image than DECODE's.

texts.label: ASMn, Archivio Gonzaga, Pandolfo Malatesta to Gianfrancesco Gonzaga, Rome, 22 Apr 1428 (DECODE R1854 image 1)

reading_review.note: Read as sentences on 5 Nov 2026: the three runs build whole Latin clauses (de suis gentibus armigeris cassandis ..., rex effici, tetendit et iterum redivit) that agree grammatically with the clear text round them; one unread sign, no word is a hole. The clear text is this project's transcription, with its own doubts.

texts.summary: Pandolfo Malatesta, archbishop of Patras, three days after the peace of Ferrara, asks his brother-in-law Gianfrancesco Gonzaga not to disband his men-at-arms until he has more news, and proposes that Gonzaga become king of the Morea, 'without risk and without great expense', citing Count Riciardo, who went there with their sister Cleofe, the Despot Theodore II's wife.
texts.note: Cipher 307 of 308 signs; the clear Latin round the runs keeps the doubts of p1_clear.md.

prior.where: Preprint by Mark Vladimir Prizmic, Zenodo doi 10.5281/zenodo.23969170 (posted 5 Nov 2026), from Satoshi Tomokiyo's 309-sign transcription of DECODE R1854 image 1; emailed to Tomokiyo and to us the same day, after our attempt closed on 14 Oct 2026. Key and corrected transcription received as attachments and applied here.

human: The owner forwarded the outside email of 5 Nov 2026 with its attachments and asked the model to review, verify and write it up. No cryptanalysis was done in that session; the earlier attempts (Sept-Oct 2026) are the solution steps before 5 Nov.
